text_fidelity_a: FOSITAN Photo Box, 24''x24''x24'' Portable Photo Studio Professional Light Box 126 LED Brightness Dimmable Shooting Tent with 8 Backdrops for Product Advertising Like Jewellery, Food, Bags, Shoes I really like this Fositan light box. I don't have enough room to keep a light box this size open all the time. But, when I'm in need of some close up photography of something related to my hobbies (I share a lot), I want to take the best pictures possible. The Fositan light box is simple to stand up or take down. It stores easily, has a carrying strap and looks like a poster folio when folded. The LED lights are great, with a clean white light that is dimmable. There's a diffuser panel that goes inside and softens the light, eliminating reflections. It has three ports that are closed with velcro. One on top and two in the front. Each port cover can be completely removed or adjusted to your liking. The backdrop panels are nice, heavy matte sheets of plastic. With a good enough range of colors to suit just about any requirements. They are held in place by straps, one at the very front of the bottom and one at the very top of the back. And, of course, if you want, you can always make your own 'custom' backdrops out of nearly any sheet material that you can trim to fit. With some objects, like the 4WD RC car I have in the pics, I am planning on getting some kind of poster that either has an outdoor theme or maybe a race track. Because most posters are glossy, you will need to go to the art store and get some clear matte spray to reduce the glare and reflections.  In those pics of the RC, you can see how well the Fositan box works. No bright glare. No shadows. Just a very cool looking RC. I am very happy with my Fositan light box. I know I will be using it for a LONG time, and getting a LOT of great pics with it. Five stars.

text_fidelity_a:
Targus Demolition Backpack Designed to Fit up to 17.3-Inch Laptop, Black (TSB220US) Though I am giving a review for this backpack, I can't come from the perspective of having used it for a while. I only received my Targus backpack yesterday, but from the looks of it I am pretty darn sure this backpack will last a long, long time. I've used MANY backpacks in the past carrying books, laptops and supplies during the time it took to earn two separate college degrees, and at my previous job of 17 years. I had to carry tools, manuals, laptops and assorted parts to calibrate monitoring equipment around my state. I was rough on the backpacks and some wore out.

I really wish I had had a backpack like this one. It's very well constructed out of strong materials, has a plethora of pockets and places to organize your stuff, and though I don't have a 17" notebook as of yet, it appears to be deep and wide and should easily fit one. There are even slots for file folders and inside zipper pouches. There are pockets on the inside and pockets on the outside. The bottom inside has a foam rubber "shock pad" that neatly folds down flat on the bottom of the backpack and is about 1/2" thick. Plus the bottom is covered in a waterproof rubbery material that should definitely help keep water from seeping up into the bag. That happened to me several times on my job with my other backpacks and it was really frustrating. It's very easy to set your backpack down on the ground not realizing the area is wet.

The shoulder straps are padded and adjustable, and it has a waist strap for extra stability. Even if you didn't use this backpack to tote your 17" marvel of technology around, it would serve well as a camper/hiker backpack. I can't wait to start using it. If something should go wrong or tear up, I will most definitely update this review telling about it, but for now I can find no fault whatsoever with it.
text_fidelity_b: Targus Demolition Backpack Designed to Fit up to 17.3-Inch Laptop, Black (TSB220US)

text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Basics Over-Ear Bluetooth Wireless Headset with Micro-USB and 3.5 Audio Cable - Black These over the ear Bluetooth earphones are just over the ear Bluetooth ear phones. They are not noise cancelling, so if that is what you want then you'd better pass on by. These are a basic Bluetooth Wireless Headphones.

Unboxing you get the headphones, and two different cords. One cord to charge the headphones (USB plug) and one cord to use the headphones outside of Bluetooth mode. I plugged them in my laptop overnight to charge it up and then took them to work to see how they would do. At work, I found out they do not cancel noise. I could still hear every single conversation around me whether music was playing or not. To drown out conversation, I would have to turn the sound way up, but I'd rather save my hearing. However, my purposes it's ok. I really just wanted the overhead head phones to indicate to people that I'm working. For some reason, earbuds just don't communicate that I'm busy. I had to use the audio cord in my mp3 (from a famous manufacturer) because I have a first generation unit that doesn't have Bluetooth ability. I felt that earbuds vs. these were no different. I decided to start with something bass inducing, so started with early 00's Hip Hop. The bass on my earbuds is better. I then worked my thru my R&B & Alternative lists, and then finally something with high pitched tones (strings) like Irish Folk. I felt that my earbuds had slightly better sound quality. However, I did not feel like was missing out on much.

Next, I brought them home and tested them out with my laptop in Bluetooth mode. Set-up was easy. My laptop has a Bluetooth icon and I just asked it to look for Bluetooth devices. After a few seconds, AmazonBasics Bluetooth Headphones popped-up. I told it to connect and then pumped up the jamz (it's always with a z). After a couple hours, I got up to adjust the thermostat on the A/C. I walked from the dining room thru the living room and into the foyer. I realized as I was walking back I still had the headphones on! I completely forgot! So, that means they are comfortable. A little heavy, but I obviously got used to it.

Finally, I tested them with my tablet (again a well-known brand) and I was not able to connect to it. I then tried to reconnect to my laptop and the laptop did not reconnect. The instructions are no good in troubleshooting this issue. So, now I have to connect via the cable all the time, which defeats the purpose. I can use the earbuds that I've been using. Plus, my laptop stopped producing sound altogether. Additionally, when they are playing everyone can hear what you listening to, so they will not be that helpful. If my son is standing next to me or sitting at the table with me, he can hear every word from my HipHop mix. Not ideal. Speaking of HipHop, another downside is that these, unlike a well-known brand with the name of a rapper/producer attached to them, do not fold up. So, they are big and bulky in your bag when you are carrying them around. I'm also afraid that something in my purse or mini backpack is going to do something to them. I also have to make sure I'm carrying a big purse to transport these around.

Pros:
-Wireless! (Don't disconnect from the device once you get it connected you'll never get it back.)
-Comfortable on the ears
-Easy set-up

Cons:
-Not Noise Cancelling
-Sound Quality could be better
-Heavy
-Does not fold up (Bulky to carry around)
-Must use the cable if you disconnect from a device. It will not reconnect.

UPDATE: The fix to my connection issue was on Pg. 6 of the instructions, but that's not how I connected the first time. Now, that I am reconnected to my laptop, the sound is like being underwater and goes in and out. So, it's tricky and sometimes you will have a set of wireless headphones, and sometimes you won't.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics Over-Ear Bluetooth Wireless Headset with Micro-USB and 3.5 Audio Cable - Black

text_fidelity_a:
Acer Aspire One Cloudbook, 11-Inch HD, 32GB, Windows 10, Gray (AO1-131-C9PM) includes Office 365 Personal – 1 year **Discontinued by Manufacturer** There's a lot of reviews already about this product. I wavered for a good while about deciding if I wanted to accept this Cloudbook for review and now kind of wish I hadn't. As far as I'm concerned, the Cloudbook is like a merging of a laptop and a chromebook with neither giving the features that are special to each one. As far as it being a computer, it runs on Windows 10 of which I have great suspicions and doubts. If you remember, I believe most everyone received an offer for a free download of Windows 10 as an upgrade from whatever Windows program they were currently using. I have read from several sources that it was offered only as a way of installing NSA spyware on your computer. We are being watched and monitored at every turn. If you don't believe me, next time you are driving take a look at all the cameras on poles along the roads and highways and tell me we aren't being surveilled. Smartphones, smart TV's, smart refrigerators, dryers and washing machines are simply ways of letting TPTB know what we are doing at all times. How many loads of clothes you washed, what you are doing in your bedroom and on and on. So, what does all this have to do with this little and cute computer? It has Windows 10 installed.

If you are o.k. with that then overall it's not a bad machine. I really miss having a disk drive to load my own personal programs and don't like having to download stuff from the internet via the app store or some other internet source. And since it is a computer but has very little space for storage, you have to have an anti-virus program. It comes with one but it's only good for 30 days and you have to purchase it or get another one. Most of your stuff will be stored in the Cloud (like a chromebook) unless you opt for a Sandisk or external hard drive. And if you buy an external hard drive for more storage why not get a regular computer instead that has more bells and whistles and possibly a disk drive?

It looks like a chromebook and I have had to put a label on it to distinguish it from mine and my kids chromebooks. I'm having a hard time getting used to Windows 10 and it takes a long time to finally get on the internet. I have taped a piece of paper over the camera lens staring me in the face - call me paranoid if you wish but I don't like people in my house uninvited. The "shift" key is way too small and I'm always missing it.

As far as specs go they're listed on the main page but here they are again for your convenience:

11.6" HD Widescreen ComfyView LED-backlit Display (1366 x 768 resolution, 16:9 aspect ratio).
Intel Celeron N3050 Dual-Core Processor 1.6GHz with Intel Burst Technology up to 2.16GHz.
Windows 10
Intel HD Graphics
2GB of DDR3L Onboard Memory.
32GB Internal Storage
Secure Digital (SD) card reader.
802.11ac WiFi (Dual-Band 2.4GHz and 5GHz).
Bluetooth 4.0
Webcam (640 x 480)
High-definition audio support.
Two Built-in Stereo Speakers.
1 - USB 3.0 port
1 - USB 2.0 port
1 - HDMI Port with HDCP support.
Microsoft Office 365 Personal 1-Year Subscription (activation code included).
2-cell Li-polymer battery pack (4200mAh).
Up to 8 hours of battery life (Video Playback).
2.54 lbs. | 1.15kg (system unit only).

If you are already using Windows 10 then it should be easy to navigate, but I feel as if I'm learning a whole new OS though I use Windows 8 on my other laptop. It only detected two of my Bluetooth devices and I have several. If you want Word processing you must redeem your card number inside the box before a certain date or else it expires. And it's all cloud based so your data is out there and not in your pc safe and sound.

I will modify this review as needed, but I have not used this computer since a few days ago and probably will not be using it much at all. I like my chromebook better for web surfing, and it doesn't require an anti-virus program because it's totally cloud based but I never use the cloud. I store the stuff I want on my old desktop or other laptop. And my chromebook has access to a word processing program without having to buy it.
text_fidelity_b: Acer Aspire One Cloudbook, 11-Inch HD, 32GB, Windows 10, Gray (AO1-131-C9PM) includes Office 365 Personal – 1 year **Discontinued by Manufacturer**

Fire Tablet with Alexa, 7" Display, 16 GB, Blue - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th) I've had my Kindle for about 6 months and I am more excited about it now than when I bought it. Adapting to the format and operation was a snap. Pros >> Cons.

Pros: I can take more books than I could possibly carry with me on vacation. The charger is good for 110-240V so I can easily recharge it, with an appropriate plug adaptor, anywhere I go. I can browse the bookstore from home and request samples to read that download to my kindle in a few seconds. I even found, sampled, and bought a book while traveling on the DC Metro. Approximately 75% of the books I'm interested in reading can be purchased in the Kindle format. I have found, read, and enjoyed books I normally would not have tried because of the ability to sample a fair amount of text before purchasing them. I am reading more e-books than I did paper books.

Cons: It is frustrating not to be able to share a good book with a friend. I wish I could organize the content into folders and sub-folders on the display instead of just having a single level directory that goes on for pages. I tried a newspaper subscription but the e-delivery was spotty and often delayed and I really didn't enjoy reading the content that way. I am spending much more money on e-books than I spent on paper books because I am buying/reading more.
text_fidelity_b: Fire Tablet with Alexa, 7" Display, 16 GB, Blue - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th)

SanDisk Ultra II 480GB Solid State Drive (SDSSDHII-480G-G25),Black I put a 480gb version in my 5 year old Lenovo T420 with Windows 10 & 8gb of memory and the thing is amazingly fast! So far I have only installed Norton AV software, Open Office and few other apps but to give you some idea on speed. the old original HDD with Windows 7 took about 5 minutes to reboot and login, plus another 10+ mins dealing with a dragging machine that was almost useless during the AV scan. This SSD take less than 45 seconds from power on to full login and the I/O for the AV has no noticeable affect on the machine's performance. If it weren't for the disk I/O activity light blinking wildly, there would be no obvious indication that the machine was doing anything.

This 5 year old laptop was destined for the recycle bin because it was horrifically slow but will now be used until Windows 10 goes EOL or there's a massive hardware failure. I had my reservations about this investment, but now I'm thrilled that I took the leap and would do it again in a heartbeat.

text_fidelity_a:
Sennheiser Momentum Headphone - Brown I am so very pleased with these headphones. I was expecting them to sound pretty good given the Sennheiser lineage, but they really set me back on my heels with the sound quality, comfort, and overall design.

Let's start with the easy one - how they look. To my eye, they are very nicely styled. Classic-looking rather than flashy. I especially like how the headband is not excessively padded -- it does not stick out when you wear them. Very elegant overall. Everything looks and feels high quality.

They also hit the mark regarding comfort. I usually have a 1 hour limit when it comes to over-the-ear headphones, in that after an hour of wearing them I've reached my limit of tolerance. These, however, felt wonderful. They are light enough that I hardly noticed the weight. More importantly, the ear cups fit me just right. Cushy enough to seal out ambient noise but not at the expense of having my ears feel like they were trapped in a vice. They felt just as good well into hour 2 as they did in the first 15 minutes. I found the headband also very comfortable for long stretches without getting "sweaty head" as I get with other headphones.

But it's the sound that counts. To my ear, these `phones deliver in spades. I started off with some Stanley Clarke. Wonderful -- ample bass but not at the expense of hearing every string being plucked. I listened to School Days a couple of times in a row, just amazed at how good it sounded. The same for Florence and the Machine -- solid, deep bass but not overwhelming.

Next up was Metric to see how vocals come through. Again, superb. I was finally able to figure out some of the lyrics on Synthetica that never came through clear enough on my ear buds. Regina Spektor was also an absolute pleasure to listen to and have all facets of her unique vocal styling come through so clearly.

I also tried them for movie watching on my Fire, and again was very pleased. Dialog was clean and pronounced; explosions were, well, explosive.

The noise isolation is quite good. These are not noise cancelling headphones, so some ambient noise will leak in, but it keeps out everything other than the most significant ambient sounds.

I really can't fault these on any criterion. They look great, feel great, and sound great. Granted, the price is not so great, but good quality costs. If you're a demanding headphone user, these are worth the money charged. Highly recommend.
text_fidelity_b: Sennheiser Momentum Headphone - Brown

LaCie Mobile Drive Secure USB-C 5TB for Apple This is a nice portable drive if you need a large drive to backup all of your files. Note that this is a magnetic HDD and not a SSD based drive, so it is pretty slow and not really ideal for use as a system drive or a work drive for large files like RAW photography, etc.. its great for backup and storage purposes though and the aluminum enclosure looks great with surface pro, macbook and other sleek metal shell laptops.

The drive runs really quiet and the aluminum enclosure does a good job of working as a heatsink to dissipate the generated heat without the need for fans or vents. Like all spinning HDD it does vibrate some when in use but not too bad. Works with both USB-C and USB 3.0 so it should work with pretty much any computer from the past 20 years or so.

Overall, great drive with an attractive enclosure and I would recommend it for backup or general storage purposes but if you need to access files quickly with higher performance I think its worthwhile to spend a little more for an SSD based drive since the prices on those have come down a lot recently.
text_fidelity_b: LaCie Mobile Drive Secure USB-C 5TB for Apple

Motorola S11-Flex HD Wireless Stereo Bluetooth Headset - Black/White The electronics and features of this blue-tooth headset can't be beat. The sound quality is second to none. Now, the bad news. The materials and construction of this headset couldn't be worse. It was just a matter of weeks before the plastic neckband starts to crack. The soft rubber skin on the inside of the neck band and ear pieces is glued on with some type of adhesive that starts to break down pretty quickly, turning into some kind of goo that releases the skin and leaves a slimy sticky mess.

I have actually purchased two of these. With the first one, I thought maybe I was too 'rough' with it and caused it to crack. But, when the second one did the same thing, I gave up, understanding that it was just an inferior product. My advice, don't spend your money on this one. Get one of those that remains around your neck with the 'ear buds' on flexible leads that dangle when not in your ears.

text_fidelity_a:
Microsoft Wired Keyboard 600 (Black). Wired Keyboard for Gaming Experience. USB Connectivity. Spill Resistant Design. I bought this keyboard as a replacement for the original one came with my HP computer which is a USB wireless. I liked the original one but it can't be used with rechargeable AA for a long time. I had to keep recharging constantly. And I didn't like the idea of wasting throw away batteries.
This new keyboard is just as compact and light as the original, it's a minimalist's dream. Key stroke is very quiet and requires very short stroke kind of like using a notepad keyboard. Plug & play operation is extremely trouble free, you'll need no instruction at all. Some of the photos I have seen showing PS2(old type connection) adaptor included but mine didn't include it, which wasn't an issue for me. There's a special key for "calc" but I didn't have a problem starting it in a couple of key strokes, so it's not a big advantage. Another feature is its "spill-resistant design". It's nothing more than a several slits under the keyboard. If you spill water, it may help drying quicker, for anything else, you'll have a hard time getting it clean, probably never completely like any other keyboard.
Over all, I like everything about this keyboard with no negative opinion. Only thing I don't know about it is its durability but from the way I feel, it seems well made and will last for a long time.
The photo showing on this page is misleading. It comes with keyboard only without a mouse.
text_fidelity_b: Microsoft Wired Keyboard 600 (Black). Wired Keyboard for Gaming Experience. USB Connectivity. Spill Resistant Design.

text_fidelity_a: Electric Compressed Air Duster & Vacuum, MECO Electric Air Blower, 4 in 1 Function Powerful 3-Gear to 90000RPM/12000PA Keyboard Cleaner, Rechargeable Cordless Air Duster for Computer/Car/Pet Hair Great little electronics duster.  Very easy to use, comes with a brush attachment and a nice little bag to keep it all in when not in use.  Used it on my key board and then went around using it on all of the gaming devices we have and it worked great! It's not for actual dusting of shelves or other items though, not that you can't try, but it doesn't work very well.  I wanted to get one of these for 2 main reasons, 1.) because I am tired of spending money on compressed air.  2.) I wanted to be able to safely dust our electronics, but also, my son collects rocks and has an entire 4-shelf bookshelf that holds oh so many rocks and a lot of times to thoroughly dust, you have to remove every rock and then put every rock back.  This is extremely time consuming and contrary to what Swiffer claims, all those dusters do is move the dust round and throw it back into the air and then re-settles where you just removed the dust from. Very frustrating.  These little blowers, while throwing the dust far away back into the air, you can blow the dust in a way where it settles somewhere else for permanent removal, we have several air purifiers throughout the house, so this helps and it blows it away from what you need it to, so that it doesn't settle right back to where you just removed it from, like a regular duster.  When I used this on the rock shelves though, there wasn't much in the way of even removing most of the dust, but that's okay, I didn't have high expectations here either.  I feel like this duster is great for electronics and well worth the money- no more compressed air cans for this gal!  Hope this review is helpful!
text_fidelity_b: Electric Compressed Air Duster & Vacuum, MECO Electric Air Blower, 4 in 1 Function Powerful 3-Gear to 90000RPM/12000PA Keyboard Cleaner, Rechargeable Cordless Air Duster for Computer/Car/Pet Hair

text_fidelity_a: Samsung Galaxy Note 10.1 2014 Edition (32GB, White) I bought tablet  a few days after release. It has super hardware specs and a beautiful screen; however, it seemed to me Samsung rushed its release in order to beat several other tablet coming to market. This Spen is great, yet the Note program needs to be refined to include a few more enhancement similar to the IOS program Notability. There are several bugs that Samsung should have addressed prior to release, and I am sure they will fix with future updates. The bezel appears to be cheap plastic, but I did like the leather back cover. The Polaris Office program is very good but lacks documentation. I returned both of the Notes I tried. One came slightly damaged and both had several software related issues. This does not mean this is a bad product but it is far from polished. I love Samsung and have owned several of their products including a two Samsung Galaxy phones and a Samsung Galaxy 5.0 Player. Their are several positives here, but as it stands now,  this is not a iPad replacement. It is not nearly polished enough and its battery life is not nearly as strong. For $600.00, it should be a lot more refined. I buy the best product from whoever makes it, and I have zero allegiance to any brand. My agenda is about work and productivity, and this product gets it done with several fixable bumps in the road.
text_fidelity_b: Samsung Galaxy Note 10.1 2014 Edition (32GB, White)

text_fidelity_a: Microsoft Arc Mouse - Black. Sleek,Ergonomic design, Ultra slim and lightweight, Bluetooth Mouse for PC/Laptop,Desktop works with Windows/Mac computers This mouse is an interesting concept.  It's a bluetooth mouse that you turn on by folding it into an arc, and turn off by flattening.  It provides easy storage, and it's easy to know whether your mouse is off or on.  The enclosed instructions with the mouse were very clear, and I had no problems setting it up and getting my computer to recognize it.  Setup was quick, too.  The mouse moves about easily, and the finger surface is basically a click pad- you can click the mouse, but you can also scroll by moving your finger up and down.  I really like that feature.  The only thing I don't really like about this mouse is that it doesn't fit very well in my hand.  Either this mouse is too big or my hand is too small.  My hand gets cramps rather quickly using this mouse.  I've not had problems with any other mouse.  While the description says "ultra-slim" it's still too wide for me, and I have adult female hands.  If there was a smaller version of this mouse, I'd like it better.
text_fidelity_b: Microsoft Arc Mouse - Black. Sleek,Ergonomic design, Ultra slim and lightweight, Bluetooth Mouse for PC/Laptop,Desktop works with Windows/Mac computers

text_fidelity_a:
Soundcore by Anker Life A2 NC Multi-Mode Noise Cancelling Wireless Earbuds, ANC Bluetooth Earbuds with 6-Mic Clear Calls, 35-Hr Playtime, and Deep Bass, Fast Charging, Transparency, and App The first couple of generations of Soundcore headphones were pretty mediocre. I'm glad the company keep improving their products. This year's models are really good for the price.

I got the Life A2 model. For $80, these earbuds come with features that I usually see on earbuds that cost more than $100 like equalization, noise cancellation, and upgradable firmware. These features all work great. I especially like the equalization that noticeably improves sound clarity.

Overall, the sound quality is great for earbuds that cost less than $100. Bass is not boomy, but great if you like a more natural sound. Stereo separation is excellent. Clarity at the higher frequencies is excellent when I set the equalizer to type of music that I'm listening too. Volume is better than average for true wireless earbuds.

These earbuds are on the larger side, but they don't stick out of my ears too much, so I don't constantly knock them out like I do with Apple-style earbuds. They are comfortable and secure enough in my ears.

I'm using an Android smartphone and the earbuds pair easily with my phone. Bluetooth connection has been solid. The Soundcore Android app is necessary to manage the equalizer and upgrade the firmware and both features work great. The app also shows your battery levels. Unfortunately, the app does spam me occasionally with unrelated Anker product announcements. I wish they wouldn't do that. Anker spams me enough by email.
text_fidelity_b: Soundcore by Anker Life A2 NC Multi-Mode Noise Cancelling Wireless Earbuds, ANC Bluetooth Earbuds with 6-Mic Clear Calls, 35-Hr Playtime, and Deep Bass, Fast Charging, Transparency, and App

text_fidelity_a:
TCL 65" Class 4-Series 4K UHD HDR Roku 2017 Smart TV - 65S405 Do not be afraid! This is a great TV.

The good: I won't go into the technical details and explanations. Others have done that for me. We purchased this for a new home and have had it set up for a couple of weeks. The integration of Roku is seamless, and it retains those same intuitive menus. It has no WiFi connectivity issues for us (we have a Google mesh network with a good signal at the TV location), and effortlessly streams Netflix, Amazon Video and You TubeTV-- DVR and live-- and looks great doing it. I haven't tried 4K content yet, so can't comment on that.

The bad: It doesn't handle low light scenes very well in movies and television, and particularly when viewed from any angle that isn't straight on. That's why I gave it four stars instead of five. If you can overcome that, forge ahead! I couldn't justify spending twice or more on Samsung or others. Another minor quibble-- silver feet on a black frame looks a little odd.

The bottom line: I was skeptical. I've owned Samsung plasma and LED and an LG LED recently and I see no material difference between the TCL and the other LEDs. All the positive reviews here, plus the CNet reviews/primers on Roku integrated TVs put me over the edge. We really like this TV and it's simplified our streaming incredibly. Go get it!
text_fidelity_b: TCL 65" Class 4-Series 4K UHD HDR Roku 2017 Smart TV - 65S405

text_fidelity_a:
Gosky 12x55 High Definition Monocular Telescope and Quick Smartphone Holder - 2018 This is a really nice optical device. I hadn't necessarily heard of Gosky before, but I gather they are a big brand in optics. I'm also going on relatively little education on the subject that a monocular is easier to focus at longer distances and/or a larger range of distances because you don't have to focus the two lenses - something which makes it hard for me to look through binoculars after a while.

This is pretty lightweight, but feels very solid and nice. It has a turn-out piece to the rear of the rear lens to accommodate people who don't wear glasses. And besides that, there is only one knob to turn to focus, mostly depending on the distance to the object of your attention.

The carry case is fairly rugged nylon and has a belt loop, but not the kind of belt loop you can use without unstrapping your belt. It's also a little large for a belt in my opinion, but may come in handy. The hand strap is pretty nice, but there is a lot of extra length to the strap I really don't know what to do with, and I feel like the actual attachment process could be more refined. I do really like that both lens covers can stay attached to the body while not in use (rear one can be attached to the hand strap and front on is attached to a rubber ring which stays on the body) which makes for a refined and complete product.

Not sure if this one can accommodate a cell phone holder or not...seems like people must take pictures through these things when birding or spying or watching opera or whatever they're doing.

Nice product. I now have a good feeling about this brand that was previously off my radar.
text_fidelity_b: Gosky 12x55 High Definition Monocular Telescope and Quick Smartphone Holder - 2018

text_fidelity_a:
SanDisk 8GB Clip Sport MP3 Player, Blue - LCD Screen and FM Radio - SDMX24-008G-G46B UPDATE: 11/15/14 Just found out that you can NOT transfer overdrive (library) WMA format books. I didn't realize it earlier because all the books I'd put on it were in MP3 format which do work fine, but some library books only come in WMA and apparently the sport only supports DRM free WMA, which means not library books.
UPDATE: 11/8/14 Wound up w/problems w/this clip & had to return for replacement. Was w/in 30 so did thru Amazon & just got new one in. Will see how it works. This happens occasionally w/clip+ & zip so not too worried. Still think the clip+ is the best, followed by the zip, then the sport.
UPDATE: 10/5/14 I have since found the Pause delay has gotten much worse than when I 1st tried it & can last way too long like others said - sometimes about 15 seconds when resuming play - which may not sound like much, but it is. It becomes very problematic in that it takes so long you don't know if you pushed play again or not. If you push it again too soon then when it finally does come on it immediately goes off again. Sometimes it's taken me up to 6 tries to get it right & that is ANNOYING! Also, it tends to go to have a delay before playing after you FFWD, which again can cause the same problem. And, as others said, the FFWD is Very Slow. Sometimes when I try to FFWD I have a pause issue & then somehow it goes back to the start of the book & then I have to start all over w/the FFWD - again - very irritating. The bigger screen seems a waste too, as the book cover is shown in a tiny square that's hard to see. In the zip it fills the whole screen & is actually bigger, so what was the point of the larger screen? I don't know who at SanDisk could actually think all these usage & design changes were good ideas, as far as I can see they've only come closer to ruining a good thing. If they wanted a new & improved clip, they should've kept all the features & workings of the clip+ & just added a larger color screen, a more durable clip (& a longer battery time is always nice), but changed nothing else. Each newer model, even the zip, but especially the sport has taken away more than it's gained. For the meantime, I've reduced it from 4 to 3 stars & must say the sport model is the worst of the 3. I'll be writing to Sansa support to see if there is some sort of software fix. If there is, I'll revise this review again.
------------------
Original Review:
Works fine with audiobooks. Read a number of bad reviews & 1 that said couldn't use with library's Overdrive Media system, but I did not have any real trouble with it. Yes, it's true, doesn't have a MSC setting, but I xfr'd books from OM w/no problems. The only difference was I normally make a new folder under audiobooks & name it w/book title, series # & author's name. When I made a new folder it wouldn't let me name it. Instead I simply chose Audiobooks, then in the first box where that showed, went in and typed a / then how I wanted sub folder to be named, then continued as usual. It make the sub folder as I named it and xfr'd the files there. When I checked my books folder, they were all there under the folders I'd named that way. I'd had this same problem once before with a clip zip, and it's not a major impediment, it's actually a bit faster, really.

With Audible, I've never been able to activate or deactivate a device, I always have to contact them to reset. Also at 1st it showed the internal drive space as the external drive space even tho no card was in the clip. I chat'd them & they logged onto my pc, activated it, renamed the drive it was showing as & now it works fine. They even fixed another problem I'd had w/Audible software crashing when I tried to delete books on any of my clips. They said the drive identification problem was specific to the clip sport, but they fixed in in almost no time & I would've had to call them regardless of which clip type I bought. It is slightly bigger, about 1/4" taller, 1/8" wider & 1/16" deeper but it's still darn small & the bigger screen makes it a bit easier to read. I haven't tried in sunlight but I can't read either the clip+ or zip in sunlight either, I just find or make some shade. I listen only to audiobooks so I can't comment on playlists or other music functions.

Re the power button, I don't have a problem w/it working, but I would prefer a separate button, don't know why it was removed. Re the pause/play delay. Yes, there is one. It's about 1-3 seconds from pressing pause & about 2-7 seconds for pressing play again. I didn't find it to be an extremely long delay, but again, would prefer they fix that issue but it's not a deal breaker for me, I just have to remember to wait those few seconds & not try pressing the button again too soon! I can see where if you are doing something where you're operating the functions w/o looking it would be irritating.

I haven't tried copying cd books that I've ripped w/windows media player, but I know that the order always gets messed up with clip zips, so I've always only used storage on micro cards with the clip+ for those books. They changed something when they made the zip & I'm guessing the sport won't be different, but I'll add a post if I find differently. I use the zip & now the sport for Overdrive & Audible. I always keep 3 clips at any given time as they tend to die in about a year of daily use (2-10/hrs per day) and any Overdrive books I've stored for them can't be put on a different clip, but they're cheap enough that works for me. The clip mechanism breaks sometimes (I have 2 working zips now w/broken clips) but I then use 2 part epoxy & glue a potato chip clip on and they don't last as long but can always glue a new 1 on as long as the clip works. Also, sometimes a clip dies & if holding down the power button for a long time doesn't work, I've found if I wait a few days sometimes then I can connect to usb on pc & it starts working again.

Yes, all clips have specific issues and the old clip+ is still my favorite and I'll always keep 1 of them that works, but for the other 2 I get what ever's on sale at the best price. I wanted an 8gb this time because I don't like to put Overdrive books on storage cards & it was only $10 more than a 4gb clip+ (for some reason their price has gone up recently). I, too, hope Sansa keeps making the clip+ because it's still the best one out there (because it can play copied cd books) but to me the zip & sport are pretty equal except for the mildly annoying pause delay, but if I can get an 8gb sport for same price as a 4gb zip, I'll live w/that! Sansa CLIPS are still by far the BEST & CHEAPEST & ONLY SMALL MP3 players that work well for audiobooks, so I'm still a loyal customer. ALSO THEIR CUSTOMER SERVICE IS VERY HELPFUL. They always replace any that break w/1 yr warranty, they help w/problems even after & sometimes can fix by updating software, etc. So for all those folks who had a problem, call Sansa before you give them a bad review! I use them for many hours every day & have for years now, so I know of what I speak. (Also, don't ask me why, but I've found the purple clip+ tends to have tighter audio jacks which cause static if headphone is not fully connected & it's harder to push jack all the way in, so just stay away from the purples - tho they will replace it if you have problems. Never had any trouble like that with black, blue or red one's.)

Yes, the developers have cheese for brains & the only 'improvement' in the newer models is larger screen w/color & graphics which can make book identification by cover image easier to figure out even if can't read type & the other changes in my opinion make them not work as well as the clip+. Those differences may not matter with music, but do for audiobooks. Each type has some flaws (& battery time is never as good as advertised, I'd say 8 hrs for clip+ & zip) but they're still better than anyone else for a no hassle, easy to use, tiny clip that you can wear w/o dragging on clothes or falling out of pockets & their prices can't be beat! I've looked & looked over the years & have never found anything better. So I still say thanks to Sansa for making the clips!
text_fidelity_b: SanDisk 8GB Clip Sport MP3 Player, Blue - LCD Screen and FM Radio - SDMX24-008G-G46B

text_fidelity_a:
Case Logic TBC-411 DSLR Compact Backpack (Black) There’s some good points to this bag, but there are also a number of limitations that keep it at a three star rating.

On the plus side, the build quality is, in usual Case Logic fashion, well done. Strong, even stitching throughout; nice straps and buckles; good quality zippers with easy to find pull tabs. It feels and looks quite nice.

Unfortunately, the overall design does not meet as high of a standard. The padding is thin throughout. While I know this is for lighter, smaller DSLRs, I did not feel it provided much security for my Canon Rebel XT with just a couple of lens (50mm and 85mm). It’s not a size issue – just to see if I could, I was able to fit in my Canon 5D Mark II with the Canon 70-200L zoom plus the hood. It’s not a size issue, but rather a padding issue. The foam is thin and is not nearly as dense and bump absorbing as packs from Tenba, Lowepro or Crumpler. Granted, this is addressing a lower price point, but it’s not that low. Other lower-end bags I’ve tried have far more robust padding.

The slot for the tablet is another issue. Great idea; poor execution. There is very little padding for the tablet – forget about putting in a tablet unless it has a hard case, since this backpack won’t offer much protection. Same for the side pockets which have no padding.

This is a good choice if you’re looking to tote very little gear and are willing to bring along the cases for the camera and lenses to aid in keeping them protected. This is not a good choice if you’re looking for a “grab and go” type of backpack. Nice looking, but poor protection.
text_fidelity_b: Case Logic TBC-411 DSLR Compact Backpack (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Mini Projector, CiBest Native 1080P Projector Outdoor, 2023 Upgraded 9500L Full HD Portable Projector, Small Home Movie Projector 200" Supported, Compatible with PS4, PC via HDMI, VGA, AV, and USB The projector works well in small rooms and projects well onto an empty wall. We had to use a binder to prop it up so the video would be high enough to watch comfortably. IF you do use a binder or another angled surface, at least one of the edges will be blurry so you'll have to adjust the keystone. Without the adjustment, think that one haikyuu scene where it zooms in on Aone's forehead as he goes to block the spike. The overall quality of the picture is fine, but the pixels could be finer because they're still kinda big. Also, the colors are not as vibrant, but they are still pretty good quality. While watching, the audio comes through the projector. IF you do use the audio through the projector, it is crunchy. I am talking crunchier than a freshly opened bag of frito's lays in a dead silent movie theater during a dramatic death scene. I would definitely suggest using an external speaker or audio output unless the projector's crunchy audio appeals to you and your loved ones.

tl;dr
could have more pixels
could have better color
definitely look into an alternative audio source
works well in small rooms
doesn't have to be super dark for the screen to show up (pretty bright)
text_fidelity_b: Mini Projector, CiBest Native 1080P Projector Outdoor, 2023 Upgraded 9500L Full HD Portable Projector, Small Home Movie Projector 200" Supported, Compatible with PS4, PC via HDMI, VGA, AV, and USB

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin nuvi 1490LMT 5-Inch Bluetooth Portable GPS Navigator with Lifetime Map & Traffic Updates (Discontinued by Manufacturer) This little device came in handy during my recent trip to San Francisco, CA. I connected my Garmin nüvi 1490LMT 5-Inch Bluetooth Portable GPS Navigator to my Toyota and it worked great. Installing and using this little machine is simple and easy. The instructions are easy to follow. I had a great time going to different places in San Francisco using this GPS and it never failed me. If you take a wrong route or direction, no problem, it will re-calculate and give the directions to get back on the right tack and keep driving. It works wonderfully. This has many features to help you get from point A to point B quickly and safely; features such as audible driving directions with text-to-speech (TTS), spoken street names, real-time traffic updates, and Internet connectivity for points-of-interest search, 5-inch resistive touch screen with colorful, animated map graphics and large easy-to-read screens are some of the coolest features. It comes complete with free lifetime map updates and traffic reports. The traffic reports are indicated pictorially using specific colors; red (heavy traffic), green (easy traffic) and yellow (moderate traffic). You do get a 3D junction view and speed limit indicators. If you are driving over the speed limit, the speed limit (e.g. 65 MPH), the display of 65 MPH goes red, if you are below the speed limit, it goes green.

It also offer robust point-of-interest (POI) search, including good category breakdowns, as well as searches that update in real time as you drive, complete with compass directions. When we were in Berkeley, CA, we were in an area which was completely new to us, and we wanted to go to an Indian restaurant and this feature helped us to find the nearest restaurant.

My brother uses GPS-enabled smart-phones and recommended me to go for GPS and I have never regretted buying this little gizmo, this offers good value for money.

Pros
* Big 5-inch screen
* Free lifetime traffic
* Pedestrian/public transit navigation
* Multi-destination routing
* Lane assist

Cons
* We had routing problems in some cases. It did not give the correct straight forward directions in my own home town. Once the satellite communication did not work when we are going to the airport.
* Traffic/lane info is available only in some cities
text_fidelity_b: Garmin nuvi 1490LMT 5-Inch Bluetooth Portable GPS Navigator with Lifetime Map & Traffic Updates (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Kingston 8 GB Class 4 SDHC Flash Memory Card SD4/8GB I ordered this part for use with a new Audibon Birdcam. The Kingston memory card failed in just over a month. It was unreadable by several PCs and a Mac. Amazon said to contact Kingston directly (Kingston memories carry a lifetime warranty). Kingston had me return the memory (my expense) and issued an RMA. They used "UPS Mail Innovations" to ship.
UPS MI is an el-cheapo service that uses the USPS mid-stream and for final delivery. Predictably, the shipment to me was lost by the USPS and tracking information abruptly stopped. It took four telephone calls to Kingston, the final call being to a supervisor, to get another parts shipped. The CS reps kept reading me the dead tracking info in which the shipment was "out for delivery" in another state and past due by several days. It's been three weeks since I sent the part back. I'm waiting for the second RMA part to arrive.
I'm not sure that Sandisk memories are fundamentally any better, but I can say that I never suffered a failure of any of their many memories I own.
text_fidelity_b: Kingston 8 GB Class 4 SDHC Flash Memory Card SD4/8GB

Belkin 8-Outlet Surge Protector with Power Cord Organizer, Designed for Office and Conference Room I have a huge Belkin surge protector in my office that meets all of my needs and also occasionally makes me lunch (it's pretty rad), but since having a baby, I've found that my definition of "rad" has changed to mean not visible, attractive, or accessible by the baby. While this isn't meant to be babyproof, I've found that the cage-like design and locking mechanism not only keep my cords tidier, but also makes them a lot less obvious and exciting to baby so that when it is placed out of reach, he isn't always clamoring to be lifted up to it, as he does with high-up cords that are not as hidden.

Two things that I don't love: One is that the sliding mechanism that opens out to allow you to put the cords in and use the diagonally-sliding plugs easily - they are a little stiff. So stiff that in fact I doubted whether I was really supposed to slide them out and was afraid I'd break the thing. I also found the locking/ opening/ closing mechanism too stiff - in fact, I gashed my finger when it opened unexpectedly after having to push it harder than I should have to open it.

The other thing is that there is no method for hanging this outlet on the wall. So I have to set it on a high shelf, which is less cool than just hanging it behind my printer or something.

Otherwise, I love that I can neaten up a decidedly un-neat portion of my office with this, and be assured of clean power to boot.
text_fidelity_b: Belkin 8-Outlet Surge Protector with Power Cord Organizer, Designed for Office and Conference Room

text_fidelity_a: Fire HD 8 Tablet, 8" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB - Includes Special Offers, Magenta (Previous Generation - 5th) I would like to give this a five rating but it is still too quirky to receive that. I deducted a star for each major problem-no control over storage and what appears to be an unstable OS. I switched from another android tablet that was giving me problems. My brother has the largest Kindle Fire HD and it looked very nice. I paid extra to get rid of the ads because they were too obtrusive. One would pop in while I was doing something and shut down that app. I wanted a device for reading e-books and listening to audio books. I also wanted something that had external storage that I could manage. Wrong. The app saves to the external storage card but the downloaded content goes directly to the device storage which makes no sense. Why have an external storage option when none of the larger content files will save to it? The sound is more treble than bass, but it sounds good. My device is only 8 GB, so it max'ed out quickly when I downloaded content. I like the thin form factor. This cuts down the amount of weight in my bag. I got the magenta with a purple cover. Maybe it is because this is the first time I am using it, but the OS is very jumpy and the screen is not as responsive as I would like. I have to tap several times to open an app or play a song. Once I figured it out, downloading from my accounts was easy. Unfortunately when I tried to view my internal content, the device went into a loop, then restarted itself and that took a long time. If I ever am able to download to my SD card as the instructions say, then I will be happy to upgrade my review. In the meantime, I am disappointed that this is not able to do what I wanted.

Canvas Laptop Backpack Shoulder Bag - College Outdoor - Fit 15" Laptop (Brown) I’m really impressed with this backpack. Given the price point, I was expecting a so-so pack with limited functionality. Instead, this backpack has quite a few well-done features, and the overall appearance is very striking.

It’s made mostly of canvas, which gives is a “broken in” look right from the start. It’s a very nice change from the usual nylon packs. The canvas is thick and sturdy, and has a great feel to it.

The build quality is impressive considering the price. The stitching is all tight and even, the zippers are of good quality, and the snaps/fasteners are all solid and durable. The strap padding is a little thin, but still comfortable. I was really pleased to see that there was padding on the back. That’s not an option I was expecting at this price. It gives the pack a much more comfortable feel when it’s loaded down.

The inside is lined with a smooth, snag-free lining that’s either nylon or poly (not 100% sure). In any case, it is also very well stitched, with no loose threads, sags or puckers in the material. It makes it very easy to slide books, laptops, etc. in and out of the pack. There are also a couple of compartments inside the pack, both zippered and open, to help organize all the little items that everyone needs to tote around. Additional pouches are on the outside of the pack, which are great for easy access. I didn't have any problem stowing all my small items inside of some type of pouch.

The size is ample for a typical laptop plus a few other items. I loaded it down with books to see if it could take the weight, and the pack performed very well.

The build quality, looks and performance make this an excellent value for the price. Well worth considering if you’re looking for a pack that won’t break the bank in terms of cost.

text_fidelity_a:
Asus Nexus 7 2B32 7-Inch 32 GB Tablet, Black (2013 Model) 7 May 2014: Thanks to Google's omission of full USB OTG function, file transfers are frustrating & sometimes impossible. When I return home, I'm rooting it.

After 24 hours, I like it. It's a little different from my Galaxy Player 5 inch. The extra processor speed is nice. So is the combination of the light weight and larger screen. The GP5 was getting bogged down by software bloat. It fits nicely in my old K3 case. So far, so good.

...and it works with my Targus Bluetooth keyboard. Actually, it works better than it does with the GP5. The Samsung has some key-mapping problems, probably due to Gingerbread.

As to reading, I happened to be starting a novel the other day, and started it on the Nexus 7. I had no problem. I did keep the brightness on 'Auto', so the light level of the screen matched the ambient light. With the GP5, matching light levels was a little chancy, so I had a bit more eyestrain. (Of course the extra 2" of screen have no bearing on that, right?)

I did try the freebie 'La Luna' video that Google gives away. It watched fine on the 7" screen. The thing I really like is that there is a 7" screen in the weight of a past-technology 5" package. I owned a Nook color for 13 days, but took it back because of the weight and balance. It just wasn't comfortable to hold.

I haven't tried any significant music listening. I suspect I'll still prefer my Clip+ for that. The Nexus is a little large for that purpose. I also haven't tried the camera in any particular serious way. A selfie and a picture of my cat isn't much of a trial. Again, I'll probably use a purpose-made camera for real pictures. I also haven't explored portability yet. In the case, it's a bit bulky for easy transport, whereas the GP5 fits in my pocket next to my cell phone. I probably won't put the N7 in my pocket without a case. It's a little large and fragile seeming for that.

...As to the camera, it's OK, the image quality is fine, but a 7" tablet just isn't a good ergonomic platform for picture taking. This is the best from an afternoon at Mass Audubon's Ipswich River Wildlife Sanctuary.

Picture is available at:
MobileRead Forums > E-Book Readers > Android Devices>Nexus 7 2013 1st Impressions

...And I still prefer my Clip+ for music. I hand to hunt around the Android store for a decent player for my collection which includes WMAs as well as MP3s. Google does not play WMAs (cue prissy, superior sniff). I settled on Poweramp, not because it was perfect, but because it was the first one I came to that was good enough. I just want to listen to some music, people, not commit my soul to a single, ringing, crystalline-pure music player that rules them all. Sheesh.

Someday I may do a better review, too. All of the usual things about tablets are at worst adequate on the N7.

Oh, one piece of free advice, worth every penny you paid: Don't go hog wild buying really great accessories. Shop around. A $3 wire easel from a craft store will make a fine desk stand. I have one at work and one at home. A chopstick and a binder clip will do in a pinch. Also, there are good $10 EVA zip cases that will protect your N7 for transport. They don't have to be purpose built. My old K3 had a case that loosely fits the N7 (freebie!) and my KPW1 lives in a similar case. As to ear buds, the candy-colored $5 ones in the bin at the cash register at WalGreens are my favorite, and you never misplace them, because candy-colored.
text_fidelity_b: Asus Nexus 7 2B32 7-Inch 32 GB Tablet, Black (2013 Model)

Pogoplug Series 4 Backup Device Pogoplug (this and other models) are an inexpensive way to have some capabilities of more expensive Network Attached Storage (NAS) devices. The most significant difference is a Pogoplug does not come with a hard drive installed. You have to supply your own hard drive as the backup drive. Mostly, I don't recommend this device, or the other offerings in the product line. The Pogoplug is just the beginning of what it will cost to get a complete backup solution with remote access and cloud storage. It's a solution sold piece-by-piece and, in the end, for the same outlay you can buy systems with better functionality and more builtin features.

If all you want is a way to backup files from multiple computers running different Op Systems (e.g. Windows and Mac OS X) to a local backup system, the Pogoplug will do that. If, however, you want to access your files when you're away from home or the office where the Pogoplug is installed, you'll need to buy their app for that from the Pogoplug website.

If you want your files also backed up to cloud storage, you have to buy that as well from the Pogoplug website. They sell 1TB storage, although it's advertised as 'unlimited' cloud storage. In my opinion their cloud storage is expensive. Consider also it takes a very long time to upload 1TB of content and, should you decide to discontinue the service, it takes a lot longer to download that same 1TB.

The best way to think of a Pogoplug is that its like candy dispensing machine. You buy a Pogoplug (the machine) and get one piece of candy free as a promotional item. You purchase more candy one piece at a time. They sell a lot of candy and It's not cheap.

There are some things I like about this item and more I do not. For example, unless you're a big customer, tech support is only available by email. It takes a couple days for a question to turn around and for that and other reasons I don't like email support. Then, too, in order to get all the features I want is an expensive proposition, since the real meaty features cost extra. While Pogoplug Backup (the app that comes with the device) works on both PCs and Macs, it has an annoying glitch on the Mac platform. Whenever a computer restarts (often with all the software updates and service packs) Pogoplug software restarts as well. On the PC, this does not trigger a full backup of already backed up files. On the Mac it does. Essentially, the Pogoplug Backup app for Mac doesn't seem to keep track of what' been backed up so you get to work on a slowed down Mac while Pogoplug needlessly does a full backup. Further, while Pogoplug Backup updates files that have been altered, it does not have versioning.

The most frustrating thing about Pogoplug is that your files are stored on the device locally, on your local network. You'd think it possible to connect directly to the attached drive to access shared files. Not so! Access to files stored on your own drive, located in your own home or office are only available to you from other computers when logged into my.pogoplug.com through their interface. Think how you'll enjoy this when your internet connection is down or their site is down or a myriad other things get fouled up!
text_fidelity_b: Pogoplug Series 4 Backup Device

Logitech Harmony 950 Touch IR Remote Control - Discontinued by Manufacturer So far this is my initial view of this remote just having downloaded the software and set up the initial action. Logitech, you guys need to have your heads examined. It's a REMOTE. I should not need a computer in the first place to set up a REMOTE. To add insult to this injury, they claim since I have macOS Catalina that their 32-bit software will not work. Ah, hello McFly? 32-bit apps?? Seriously? The 20th century called, they want their tech back. We've been using 64 bit for at least a decade. It is 2020 now. You know... Unbelievable. If you can't write software, fold it all up and go home. You don't deserve our money.

First mistake by Logitech. Ultimately, there IS a 64-bit app. So why do you still have a message on your web site saying we'll need an update? Here's a tip for you guys. YOU CAN JUST SUPPLY the 64-bit app right there on that screen. You could easily say for Catalina and above, click here, else get the older, lamer, 32-bit version. I have to click on a link, which seems to tell me you don't have it, which goes in a bit of a circle, before ultimately telling me that you do in fact have it.

Next, the 950 has this super stiff cover for the Micro USB connector, also technology from the cretaceous period. I think we found one of these cables in the mouth of Coleophysis bauri remains from 250 million years ago. I wasn't sure if I was breaking the thing or pulling off a cap. You software asks if I have a hub for my remote? I bought it, I didn't build it. I have whatever came in the box. Is it a hub, a charging cradle, a spacecraft, an anti-gravity device, a floatation device? I don't know. All I know is I put the device in that thing and your software doesn't detect it. So I proceed to PRY off that cap, hoping it was a cap, and it is. It would be nice if the TINY manual said so.

Before I actually try to use this thing, one more note for you brainiacs at Logitech. It would super if you made the remote with a flat back. I'll give you a guess why I say this. When you make a rounded back, us, meaning your customers, can't leave the remote on a flat surface and press the buttons without it wobbling all over the place. It pretty much becomes a two-handed operation. As luck would have it, I have two hands. But you never know. It would be super if I can just put it on a flat surface and USE it while it sits on the hard surface of, say a coffee table or nightstand.

At this stage, I'd give zero stars if possible. Hopefully the remote can redeem itself in practice. But all this nonsense to get using it in the first place is almost a deal killer. In fact, I'd bet that alone is a deal killer for many.

More to follow.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Harmony 950 Touch IR Remote Control - Discontinued by Manufacturer

PC Goose Neck Microphone, Computer Microphone With Mute Switch and Stand, Plug And Play 3.5mm Microphone For Desktop/Laptop/iPad/Tablet This product might be the best microphone since Marconi but it didn't work for me. I bought this because the Mac Pro doesn't have an internal mic. Amazingly it also doesn't have a mic port. It has 3.5 mm headphones and speaker ports. I thought I could plug this into one of those ports. No luck.
The headset port apparently requires a 4 conductor 3.5 mm TRRS plug. Neither the computer maker nor the mic/headset maker ever give you this type of critical information. I probably should have purchased a USB mic instead. So now I either buy a USB mic or a USB adaptor.

My general comment about microphones and headsets is that the descriptions (both Amazons and the manufacturers) are almost always weak on connectors, adaptors and compatability (PC/MAC/etc). This is the most important feature and should be at the top of any description. After all if it doesn't fit or work what good is it.

text_fidelity_a:
Archos 9 PC Windows 7 Starter Tablet (Black) Taken for what this is supposed to be, this is a fabulous machine. It's not a primary computer. It's not a laptop replacement. If you need a low power/ultra-portable computer, go with a netbook.

This is more of a mutt. It's a portable media player that doesn't have as much storage as an iPod or a Zen, but has a larger, higher quality screen and a kickstand, which makes it easier to watch movies at a desk.

It can read ebooks. It's not quite as light or comfortable for long term reading as a Kindle, but it can support full color images. It's far superior for this purpose than any of the other devices Amazon has put out an app for.

It can run Windows 7. It's not a full powered machine, but it's even smaller than a netbook.

It fits a slot somewhere between a PDA/smartphone and a netbook, and it's brilliant.

I would have liked a larger hard drive, an SD card (it would have gotten 5 stars if it had one) and more than one USB slot. There is no ethernet port. It only connects wirelessly. The optional port replicator gives you Ethernet and two more USB slots, but still no SD.

A few things to keep in mind. When you're first setting it up, you can't access the virtual keyboard button, so you need to use the Ease of Access icon to get to that. Windows will say to press the space bar to activate the feature. Use the mouse click button (marked +).

The design is very sleek. It's comfortable to hold and work with. The screen has an adjustable brightness, which is easier on the eyes, and easier to use in bright sunlight. The low glare screen helps with this as well.

Overall, this is bleeding edge, early adopter technology.
text_fidelity_b: Archos 9 PC Windows 7 Starter Tablet (Black)

Logitech Wireless Anywhere Mouse MX for PC and Mac, black To be honest, I'm really tired of these mice failing.

They work great at first, then eventually quit scrolling or, worse, get stuck in scroll mode and drive the cursor to the bottom of the page for no reason. Two have failed on me. The first was purchased in 2011 for $36, the second in 2014 for $30. Both failed to scroll reliably and made using them impossible. Other, cheaper, wireless mice work better, or at least longer.

This mouse has nice features like left/right scrolling by tilting the scroll wheel and they work on many different surfaces, but those features fall by the wayside if the thing doesn't work at all after some time.

I've tried blowing it out with compressed air to clear debris, but it didn't fix it. Haven't come to taking it apart and cleaning it, as some proffer, because it's simply not worth the time.

For how much these mice cost -- $66 for the two -- they should be bulletproof. Better to buy cheaper wireless mice and throw them away when the fail.

I'm trying the $11 [[ASIN:B074DV98R7 VicTsing 2.4G Wireless Mouse Wireless Optical Laptop Mouse with USB Nano Receiver, 6 Buttons,5 Adjustable DPI Levels,15 Months Battery Life]] next. I could have purchased six of them for what I've put into Logitech MX Anywhere mice, both of which become landfill fodder.

Logitech has lost my Anywhere MX mouse business.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Wireless Anywhere Mouse MX for PC and Mac, black

ASUS ZenPad 3S 10 9.7" (2048x1536), 4GB RAM, 64GB eMMC, 5MP Front / 8MP Rear Camera, Android 6.0, Tablet, Glacier Silver (Z500M-C1-SL) As a long-time Apple user, I am strongly considering other options because of a number of issues, including software updates that slow to a halt older devices ("planned obsolescence" is what they call it). Between that, the higher cost, and a few other things, I'm in the market for a different tablet and computer.

In the past, the problem switching back was that, unlike with Apple, things were not quite as user friendly with the interface and you had to really figure things out instead of it being immediately apparent.

Happily, it was different with this tablet. Out of the box, my family and I were able to figure it out quickly and easily, giving us hope in another option.

Quality: Great image on the screen with very high resolution! The feel of the device is also sturdy, aesthetically pleasing, lightweight, and thin.

User-friendly layout, very accessible, good features, and it works seamlessly with Google. I've got google email and YouTube channels, so it's nice to know there's a trade-off for losing some of the other things like seamless transitions between iTunes, my current calendar (not in love with that--I can just as easily switch to google or droid for this)...

All this adds up to the following: Apple can no longer claim to be the clear leader in tablets, phones, and computers. They have stopped innovating far beyond comparable products, and now, for the value and overall performance, the ZenPad is a worthy adversary.

I still have my MacBook Pro computer, but when it comes time to buy a new one, I will be ready to switch knowing items like these are available.
What a great surprise!
text_fidelity_b: ASUS ZenPad 3S 10 9.7" (2048x1536), 4GB RAM, 64GB eMMC, 5MP Front / 8MP Rear Camera, Android 6.0, Tablet, Glacier Silver (Z500M-C1-SL)

Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo, Full-Sized 2.4GHz Wireless Keyboard with Comfortable Palm Rest and Optical Wireless Mouse for Windows, Mac OS PC/Desktops/Computer/Laptops I've used much worse keyboards and mice, but I've also used much better. The keyboard is not bad, but speed typists would definitely prefer better. Because this is a full-size keyboard, be aware that you'll need ample space on your pull-out keyboard drawer. Some office desks have very narrow and shallow drawers. The mouse is okay too but feels a little cheap. However, this product was obviously not intended to be top-end.

My main criticism of this package is the somewhat confusing owner's manual. Every USB product I've used, particularly a kb or mouse, are plug-and-play. The manual gave instructions for "repairing' with the device, and it was unclear why you would need to issue the series of key commands in order to reconnect via USB on a PC. Perhaps this connection procedure applies only to other types of devices. After one brief failed attempt to connect (see next paragraph), the second try connected okay after I plugged in the USB dongle. I also unplugged/replugged the dongle and it worked again, without having to issue any of the "Esc + K" keypresses that the manual stated were necessary to repair the devices.

I suspect the range of this pairing is not very far. The first time I plugged the dongle in, neither the kb nor the mouse worked. I had to move both closer to the dongle before I got them to connect. The kb and mouse were only four feet from the dongle when I first installed them. After I finally got everything to connect at close range, I moved the kb and mouse back to the distance of four feet, and they continued to work. So I'm not sure of what distance would cause a disconnect.
text_fidelity_b: Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo, Full-Sized 2.4GHz Wireless Keyboard with Comfortable Palm Rest and Optical Wireless Mouse for Windows, Mac OS PC/Desktops/Computer/Laptops

So, seeing this was a Philips one – I honestly thought I lucked out. I was going to give my old cable to my mom as hers was cracking near the "C" port. I figured I could use this one - she could have my old one.

It is a DURABLE cable and looked like it would go through quite a bit. The length is perfect for charging with an adapter connected to a power strip on the floor. And, it can also plug into the USB ports on a computer (or so equipped power strip).

So, why a one star rating?

This does not work. I tried with my phone and my mom’s phone. NADA. Nothing. I tried connecting it to the adapter – nothing. Tried using just the USB cable to a USB port on a power strip (which was on since it is powering my computer) – NOTHING.

So, I tried using a USB port on my computer. NOTHING. Tried with a “USB hub” connected to my computer. There was a slight problem. The “buttons” on the port light up when a port is turned on. Despite the port for this cord being on – the lights didn’t light up. Other items connected – my external mouse and a USB flash drive – they were turned off when this cord was connected.

Needless to say – this is BELOW one star. It doesn’t even work. But, I do have to rate it something.

I could’ve gotten a bad cable – after all, there is no damage to it or the packaging. But, it still doesn't work. But, I can’t return it since it was free.
text_fidelity_b: PHILIPS 3 Ft. USB Type C Cable, USB-A to USB-C Red Durable Braided Fast Charging Cable, Compatible with iPad Pro, MacBook Pro, Samsung Galaxy S21/S10/S9/Plus, Google Pixel 5/C/3/2/XL, DLC5203RA/37

CyberPower CP1350AVRLCD Intelligent LCD UPS System, DISCONTINUED * SEE NEW UPDATED MODEL CP1350AVRLCD3 * A UPS is one of those products you don't give much thought to until you are in a situation where you REALLY need it to work. The display on the Cyberpower is a great feature - tells you all sorts of useful info such as your battery status, run time, load level and others so you always know what's going on.

Nice footprint, puts out very little heat (compared to a Tripplite that this replaces which threw off a huge amount of heat - nice in the winter time, but not so nice in the summer), simple setup. My only complaint, and the reason it lost one star, is the spacing of the outlets. You have to use outlet extenders if you have the "wall wart" transformers. I have three of them (modem, router and external hard drive) - they all fit on the Tripplite since it offers widely spaced outlets, but couldn't fit them into the Cyberpower without extenders.

The other nit is the location of the power button. It's right on the face of the unit, and you have to be careful not to hit it accidentally. A better design would be to either locate it somewhere else or, better yet, put a safety lock on it so you can ensure you don't power down unless you truly want to do so.

Both are minor issues and can be easily worked around. I'm very pleased with the unit so far, and recommend it to anyone looking for a good UPS and a nice price.
